utterances.text: Yes, I can, in view of the fact that in the area of our municipality there was only infantry weapons. There was no shelling, and then the shells that fell on our area came from the direction of the north, from Kupres, and these were fired by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The last passage of this document refers to this. I heard your answer when you said you were with the home guards. Are you aware of these events? I'm being told that I didn't give the number of document. 2D 01427. 2D 01427. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the last paragraph, it says - and I am repeating that I know that you said you were with the home guards, but maybe you are aware of this event: "The work of representatives from the HVO and the army of BiH in the presence of UNPROFOR continued in Gornji Vakuf. The realisation of the plan is being followed. Some settlements (Croatian and Muslim) have received food. Both sides presented their plans for the normalisation of life in the city with the emphasis on measures which are to be undertaken by civilian bodies. Plans are being discussed today, and tomorrow they will be adopted." So it says: "Our representatives Begic and a representative of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina Cikotic visited the location today, and they found a massacre in the village of Rojska to be true, and they found slaughtered bodies of Franjo and Finka Okadar in their home." Do you remember this specific incident? Were people talking about it, and do you remember that there were any such situations of crimes committed against Croats in the January and February of 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this event perfectly well. Unfortunately, it is true that in the settlement of Rojska, which was an ethnically pure Muslim settlement, the Okadar family was massacred. People took photographs -- the people who took photographs and later buried them told me about this, specifically Mr. Vuka Spelin [phoen].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't quite get the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name of this person who told you about this.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Luka Sekerija, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now it's correctly written, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to point out that all these questions of mine referred to the attacks in January of 1993 by the BH army, and they referred to chapter 65 and 66 -- counts 65 and 66 of the indictment. I will now continue with the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, were you aware that negotiations went on in Geneva in January 1993 and that an agreement or a joint statement was issued signed both by Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban on the cessation of hostilities between the BH army and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware of the Geneva negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Will you now look at document P 01329, which is the next document. It is the joint statement by Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, signed in Geneva, when they are ordering that fighting between the BH army and the HVO be stopped immediately. They call on the Croats and Muslims to give their full support. And in number 2: "Commanders of the BH army Main Staff and the HVO Main Staff..." May I just read it out until the end? " ... must immediately determine the responsibility for the outbreak of the fighting at all levels and form a Joint Command without delay."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Prosecutor. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Sorry. Thank you. Before counsel and the witness goes into this document, the question asked right before the document was shown to the witness actually had two portions: 1, "Were you aware that negotiations went on in Geneva in January 1993..." which the witness answered, I believe; and "Were you aware that an agreement or a joint statement was issued signed by..." et cetera, and I do not think that that part of the question was answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Nozica. Please ask the witness to specify whether he was aware of the agreement or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think if we show the witness the document, he will give us the same answer as he has said up to now. He will tell us that he hadn't seen the document. So my question is whether he was aware of the joint statement or not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard on the radio that such a joint statement was signed by Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, let me now ask you about your own knowledge. We see that such a statement was signed and an order issued to the Main Staff of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Main Staff of the HVO as early as the 27th of January, 1993, to immediately cease hostilities and to establish the course of the conflict. Were you aware that the HVO did endeavour for the conflict to be ended by negotiation as soon as possible which the HVO had not provoked? Did you know that the BH army and the army leadership was opposed to the peaceful settlement of things and that actually in those days there were already plans to attack the HVO in the entire area where the HVO was situated and that the army from this time on wanted to resolve the set-up or the structure of Bosnia-Herzegovina by war and not by peaceful means?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that I didn't have any such knowledge, but if I may, a couple of sentences related to this statement and our municipality. On the 27th of January, 1993, the Croatian Defence Council endeavoured to cease hostilities, and there were no serious attacks by the HVO. In other words, the HVO -- had the HVO had a plan or desire to take the HVO, they could have chased them out by throwing stones at them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mean the BH army could have been chased out in this period or even before this period that the statement refers to?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement is dated the 27th of January. Yes, but even before this period the HVO had control of all the more important elevations around Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But I asked you something quite different, not about the behaviour of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was -- I told you, I'm not aware of the plans and intentions of officers of the BH army, whether they were ready to implement this joint statement on non-aggression and truce. I just said that this was the intention of the HVO as confirmed by the situation before this date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll show you the following document so that we can confirm something you yourself said. It's 2D 00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. I have a question I would like to put to you with regard to this last document and in relation to the document that was examined a while ago. P 1102, if I'm not mistaken. The last document signed by Boban and Zeljkovic [phoen] shows three things, first of all. There's the combat between the ABiH and the HVO, and in fact, it goes to the benefit of the aggressor, to the Serbs. That's how we should understand it. The second thing is that the commanders of the ABiH and the HVO are asked to determine immediately who is responsible for the fight at all levels. So both parties are asked to determine who started the attack. And then the third item, Boban and Izetbegovic inviting people to set up a Joint Command. When one has a look at this document, a reasonable Judge could believe that Mr. Boban and Mr. Izetbegovic were discovering that there had been fighting ongoing, but when we see the first document, when we have a look at the first document, the 12th of January report from the Ante Starcevic Brigade, which seems to show that the ABiH launched an attack, because we see that there were 3.000 ABiH men in the field when we make the calculations. So in your opinion, wouldn't there be someone who is not telling the truth, in particular with regard to the 11th of January attack? What is your opinion, you personally? What do you think about this as you were on the ground, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday I said that I didn't know how the conflict on the 11th of January started; and today, I said that on the 12th of January the places referred to in this report from the Ante Starcevic Brigade to the HVO, well, it's a fact that the places mentioned here correspond to the way in which these places were inhabited by certain peoples. How many ABiH men there were in these inhabited places is not something that I can confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 11th of January, in your opinion, is it the ABiH that attacks the HVO or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who attacked whom on the 11th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You don't know. Very well. Ms. Nozica, you have used up almost 30 minutes. According to my calculations, each team should have 24 minutes, so someone must have given you some time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we haven't shared out our time. I'll finish with this document now. I'm surprised the fact that I've used so much time. I'll conclude with this document, 2D 00207. It's a document I asked the witness to have a look at. Yes, Your Honours. I'd just like to tell you that I was told that only three Defence teams will have cross-examination. That means three Defence teams have 40 minutes, so I'm within the limits of my time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you a question, and you said that you didn't know what the plans of the ABiH were. This document is dated the 20th of January. You said that you knew that were ongoing negotiations in Geneva and this document was signed by Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. It's addressed to the Command of the Bugojno Defence headquarters. I'll read it out to you: "We appreciate your thoughts and suggestions, but we would like to draw your attention to the execution of the tasks within the zone of responsibility. Do not engage in work that is not in your sphere of responsibility. Write reports so that they reflect the combat situation and not so as to give political lessons." And then it says: "It's premature for clashes in all the cities of the HZ HB, even though this is a possibility that has been anticipated." And then the last sentence: "Try to do all you can and help Vakuf." We're talking about the 20th of January, so this was later on when you had already joined the HVO. Did you have any information according to which HVO units from Bugojno had come to assist ABiH units in Gornji Vakuf [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. ABiH units from Bugojno participated in the combat against the HVO in the area of the Gornji Vakuf municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That would be all. I have now concluded my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. And now for the following Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I thought my colleague Ms. Alaburic was going to cross-examine. Mr. Praljak has some questions for this witness given his military knowledge; and in particular, because in the examination-in-chief these were matters addressed, we'd like to use this witness to check up on information on the deployment of forces on the front facing the Serbs. With your leave, Mr. Praljak would like to put these questions to the witness. Yesterday in the transcript with regard to the event of the 11th of January, 1993, well, this event was mentioned on page 26, and that subject was again addressed by my colleague Senka. There was a discussion about locations, about Defence lines on pages 40 and 44, and the map was entered, IC 00878.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't mean to interrupt counsel, but just a clarification with the transcript maybe before we go into the new cross-examination by a new Defence team. The latest exchange between Counsel Nozica and the witness referred to, on page 52, line 11: "Did you have any information according to which HVO units from Bugojno had come to assist ABiH units in Gornji Vakuf?" And I was wondering if that was a translation error or if it's correct that the question would be as to HVO assisting ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you clear this up or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Sorry, the page number was wrong, I believe. It's 57. 57, 12, I believe, is where the sentence should be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I understood the question from Ms. Sokolovic [as interpreted], well, she asked me whether the forces of the ABiH from the municipality of Bugojno had assisted the ABiH forces in the conflict in the month of January in Gornji Vakuf. I confirmed that because we had a lot of information to this effect. Forces from the ABiH, from the area of Bugojno municipality participated in the January conflict in an active manner in fighting in the area of Gornji Vakuf against the forces of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to thank my colleague. I think that's how I put the question. Obviously, there was a mistake in the transcript. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Praljak, you have the floor since we're dealing with military matters here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Batinic.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is it true to say that we know each other from that time in Gornji Vakuf, in Uskoplje?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, before we start dealing with maps, what does the word "Vakuf" mean?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vakuf is a religious or humanitarian association that has to serve Islam or Islamists, that simple.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: According to your information, apart from the upper part of Vakuf and the lower part of Vakuf, is it true to say that it was a kind of contract in which the inhabitants of the place at the time of the Osmanlijes had to work for religious purposes?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. In Bosnia and Herzegovina, there are several Vakufs, or there were several Vakufs. There was Gornji Vakuf; there was Donji Vakuf, Skender Vakuf, Herze [phoen] Vakuf. I won't go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And today, you live in the area now. Do we have two names for the place, Uskoplje and Vakuf Gornja?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The High Representative for Bosnia-Herzegovina decided on the 1st of October, 1991 -- 2001, that the municipality would officially be called Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Since we're dealing with this matter, does this also apply to Prozor-Rama?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but with the case of Prozor-Rama the decision was taken earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's clarify something since this question was put. What does the coat of arms and the flag of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina look like today? My question is, does it also contain the historical coat of arms of the Croatian people, the red and white checker-board?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Can you explain for the sake of the Chamber what the flag of the Central Bosnian county looks like, the county you live in? Does that flag contain the historical coat of arms of the Croatian people?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure how I could describe the coat of arms of the county of Central Bosnia, but the coat of arms and the flag for Central Bosnia are a political compromise between the Croats and the Muslims, and it contains a symbol that shows that the Croatian people live in the area too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's have a look at the maps and photographs now. Number 3D 03250. They will help us --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, could you repeat that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: 3D 03250. It's not a problem. We'll find them now. 3D 03250. It says 3D 37-0428. That's what it says at the top. That's the first one. It was a photograph from Podova. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: You're familiar with this. We'll get through it quickly. As a result, we have certain photographs here taken from the Podovi location - that's what it says - and we have Voljice, Gaj, and Jagnjid. Is this map correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have a look at the following page. The following page, 3D, and then instead of 28 at the end, we have 29 at the end. This is a place that you have marked as the location of the repeater. It's above the town of Vakuf itself. It's an elevation. Can you see that elevation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Here we have photographs that were taken this year, last summer. These are the ruins of a bunker that are still -- that are still there. My question is as follows: Before the conflict broke out in January 1993, as far as you know, did the ABiH set up bunkers at all the important elevations around the town of Uskoplje itself?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. With your leave, I'll say that this happened for the first time on the 20th of June, 1993 [as interpreted], in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, do you know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If you excuse me. Mr. Batinic, it's surprising that you can choose the exact time. Can you explain why you know so exactly that it was the 20th of June in the afternoon? Have you been directly involved or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on the 20th of June, 1992, a meeting was held in the Radusa Hotel, a meeting chaired by Mr. Muhamed Palalic and myself. We both chaired the meeting. And when the meeting came to an end, about 1400 hours, and when I went home for lunch, my brother stopped me in front of the hotel. He pointed to an elevation called Zvizde, and he said, "You're discussing things with them in a normal manner. You're functioning in a normal manner. Why are they digging trenches?" On the 20th of June, 1992, members of the TO dug a trench on Zvizde. This position was facing the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. What is striking is that in your earlier answer, which is on page 61, line 23, you said it was the 20th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: The defendants are not having the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And besides, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. Technical problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: -- there was an error in transcript. I followed. The witness said 1992, but it was 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. Although this is not sworn, I take your testimony to be the full truth. Thank you. Then my intervention is not of such interest in that case that it is worth going back and answering. So it's 1992. Thank you. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, are you testifying -- or I have another question in connection with the trenches. Are you aware that after this, after they started digging trenches, on several occasions there were discussions, and especially in December 1992, between the commander of the HVO for Gornji Vakuf and the commander of the ABiH in Uskoplje that these trenches should be filled in and that they have no military meaning in view of the positions towards the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That resulted from the incident between the 24th and 25th of October, 1992; and from then until December, those trenches remained unfilled.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So do you agree with the map that you are looking at now? So this is a photograph towards Gornji Vakuf. Can you testify to the correctness of this map and the photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The map corresponds to the actual situation on the ground. From my own house I can see clearly, which is about 300 metres as the crow flies, the remnant of these trenches with concrete in them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please turn to the next page. It is -0430. And look at the military map first. There are three red arrows. So we are now facing from the repeater, the position of the repeater facing the other side, and we're taking photographs of a locality called Mackovac and these slopes towards the ski-runs. Does this correspond to the reality?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Mackovac via Kuk towards the area where the relay was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now look at the photograph at the bottom of the picture. You can see remains of the trenches, and we know how many trenches there were around Vakuf and how good they were in quality.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about these trenches from members of the HVO, and this happened much later after the war that these trenches were very well fortified [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We can go on to the next map, again, 3D 370431. It is the next page. Again, it's 3D 03250, and the page is 3D 370431. 0431. So I just have the following question: In your view, the photograph that we see on the top, was it taken from the position of the repeater? It seems rather far removed, but tell me what you have already said, whether the -- whoever controlled the repeater and the rest of this hill, was he able to have control over the entire town of Uskoplje and especially the road from Rama via Uskoplje to Bugojno and further on?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So the question again, if --

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: Thank you. I see there is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... that I have on my screen, but it's in B/C/S, and I can't see a translation. Could we have that read out, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: There is a translation in the same file. You should see it. And, Your Honour... [Interpretation] While I'm on my feet, on page 64 in the witness's answer, 3, 4, 5, maybe there's an error in the transcript. The answer has not been properly recorded. According to the transcript, he heard about those trenches from members of the HVO, and this happened much later after the war, that these trenches were very well fortified. He said that he heard about this after the war that the trenches were well fortified at the time; whereas according to the transcript, it would appear that the trenches were fortified after the war. Maybe the witness could clarify this, when he heard about those trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Praljak, can you ask the witness to clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, tell us, when did you learn or did you know that there were constant talks, and these were particular intensified in December 1992, about the fact that the ABiH army had dug trenches at all the important elevation points in town and around the town and the HVO demanded that these trenches be filled in because they are a threat to the HVO, whereas the lines of the common enemy were five or six kilometres away towards Radusko? Did you have any knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, General. This was discussed, and I said that after the incident of October, the 24th, 25th of October, there were trenches dug around town, and the representatives of the HVO demanded and requested from the representatives of the command of the ABiH that these trenches be filled in.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Look, now, at the next page. I don't have to give you the numbers. You will see a marking saying the Partisan cemetery. The photograph was taken from the position of the repeater and the confrontation line between the HVO and the ABiH going towards the west. Is this the correct position that -- of the Partisan cemetery?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is the exact location of the Partisan cemetery or Glavica as we call it, which is at a lower elevation than the relay station.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at the next image, please. I wish to point out that these photographs were taken last summer, and it says: "From the top of the repeater in the direction of the Partisan cemetery, along the whole ridge there were shelters in the third degree, and some were even built and cemented." So these are photographs taken 16 years later. My question, again, is, if not at the time, did you know after the truce that one of the main thing was to fill in the trenches, to separate the forces, and that these trenches were fortified in a highly professional manner?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not visit these locations, but from members of the HVO after the cessation of hostilities, I heard how well-fortified the positions of the ABiH were at the elevation point that you're referring to; and long after the war, hunters would make similar comments as they moved around these areas.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, please look at the next photograph. It was taken from the position of the Partisan cemetery. Does this correspond to your own geographic knowledge of the town you live in? Is this correct? So it's from the Partisan cemetery towards the repeater and towards Uskoplje. According to your own topographic knowledge, would you agree that the repeater has full control of the entire area of Uskoplje?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: We will move on quickly now. Please look at the next photograph of the town. The photograph was taken last summer. So will you just tell me in view of the fact that you are familiar with your town, do these photographs correspond to the reality in your town?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next photograph. We here see the ski-runs, the Partisan cemetery or Glavica as you call it. Is this a photograph that has been correctly marked?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Again, we see the ski-runs on the next photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: On the next photograph, we see the elevation of the Partisan cemetery in relation to the town of Uskoplje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Now, then, we have photographs of the remains of the bunkers, which shows that they were fortified with concrete elements. Look at all the photographs one after another, one, two, three, four. I'll give you the numbers. We have to give you the numbers. Let's look at photographs number 3D 37-439. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Not this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have a question. I have a question on this. Witness, have you ever seen this? Have you been there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said, Your Honour, that the first trench that was fortified next to the repeater is something I can see from my own house every day, but I didn't see all the others because I never went to see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I -- I see a couple of broken concrete pieces that could be fallen columns or a wall or whatever. How can you say this is a bunker -- or was a bunker? Could it not be the ruins of a house, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 200 to 250 metres below this bunker that we see now was my own position at the beginning of the January conflict as a member of the armed forces of the HVO. I know very well how they acted from this area where the repeater was, and then they also built a strong -- stronghold there, and that is why I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Trechsel, we will be having witnesses on this issue who actually saw this, but no houses are allowed around the repeater, anyway. I just wish to tender these photographs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Let's go on to the next photograph, which is 0440. 440. Next one, please. I will leave out the other photographs. There's no need to burden you with these. We'll stop with the photographs there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a small question of a technical nature. The picture that we see, which according to Mr. Praljak is a former bunker, I am surprised not to see any metal reinforcements. How can you explain that? Or maybe at the time there were no metal rods.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the general said that this photograph was taken last year, so 14 and a half years after the conflict which occurred in Gornji Vakuf. At this location, I can confirm that the TV relay or repeater was situated with equipment to monitor the TV signal of Bosnia-Herzegovina television. After the combat operations and after the HVO gained control of these elevation points, the repeater was destroyed and the remaining iron rods were collected by people who wanted to sell them. They could be sold for a good price in those days.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, this flat area has elements of a good structure. Let's look at the last photograph, 0445, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Witness, look at the road down there. Can you see in the forefront? This was taken this year, this summer, not last year, the remains of a bunker facing a road. Can you see the road down there?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: From this bunker or one of these bunkers, is it possible to have full control of the road leading from Uskoplje to Rama?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because it is some 300 metres as the crow flies away.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Could we now -- can we now show Mr. Batinic a map, the number of which is 3D 00464. 3D 00464. Mr. Batinic, I'm sorry it's so small. It's not very clear, and that's not good, but I have the map here, so -- you have the map. Good. Well, have a look at it. Naturally, you weren't in the brigade command. You weren't in the command of the operative zone, and I don't think you can know everything about this. But here in red, you have the positions of the ABiH and of the HVO, the positions facing the army of Republika Srpska. That's how we'll call it. These are the red lines and the circles that you can see. So has this been correctly depicted, the line towards Bugojno and Uskoplje and further on?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really am not familiar with these topographic maps, but if this represents the defence line on the Radusa mountain from Idovac, from the area of Rama and of Raduski Kamen and then down towards Bugojno, then yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: That's what it says here. It says Raduski Kamen and Idovac and so on and so forth. That's correct. Have a look at this map, now, where we can see the lines of contact between the HVO and the ABiH around Uskoplje and in Uskoplje after the conflict had broken out. As far as you know, given the villages you are familiar with, after the conflict broke out, would these be the lines? Green is for the ABiH and red for HVO.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General, I apologise, but I can't see the inhabited places here. Perhaps you could help me. Perhaps you could mention some place names.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Well, yes. You would need a magnifying glass. Unfortunately, I didn't bring one with me. Have a look at the area around the repeater and the continuation here. In this area, did the ABiH have previously fortified positions as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning of this mountain and up towards the repeater and when you look in the direction of Rama or Pidris, yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me one more thing. Do you know that on the road from Bugojno to Travnik there was a Mujahadin camp? Did people discuss this? Did you have any information about this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, according to the information that I had when the HVO lost Bugojno and when they left Bugojno, Ravno Rostovo, a position between Bugojno and Novi Travnik, there was a motel, and the Mujahadin were located there, and according to certain information, strange things would happen there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember that at one point in time they captured -- I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOE
utterances.text: I'm asking for time specifics on this. That goes both to the question and the answer relating to Mujahadin. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: My first question: Do you know that in the conflict in January, the conflict between the ABiH and the HVO in Uskoplje, there was a Mujahadin camp in Ravno Rostovo?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: In January 1993, do you perhaps know that at that very same check-point when going to talk to the ABiH, a Croatian military delegation was disarmed with the deputy chief of the Main Staff, a Colonel Mangric [phoen]? They were stripped, looted, and they had to continue towards Bugojno while naked.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that later on, but at the time I didn't know about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have an IC -- but it's a 3D, so it's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: A few more questions. Tell me the following: The shelling of the Serbs, did this take place before the conflict that broke out between the Armija and the HVO in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They started shelling our municipality on the 15th of August, 1992. They launched the first eight shells.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: So they started this in 1992. Is it true that they killed the civilians, too, and they --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the -- could Mr. Praljak please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak is kindly asked to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the beginning of the conflict in 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. Stop, stop, stop, stop. We must go back. The question of Mr. Praljak should be repeated, and then we go on because the interpretation then stopped. So if you would like, kindly repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, my question is as follows: When the Serbian forces started shelling Uskoplje -- well, first of all, did they do that? When did they do that? When shelling Uskoplje, were there civilian victims as well? Were buildings that supplied electricity destroyed and so on and so forth? Tell us everything you know about this.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of August, 1992, in the evening hours the first eight shells were launched from Serbian guns from the area of Kupres or from Mali and Veliki Siver, as our soldiers called it. They fell on the Croatian part of town or, as I said, that's how they greeted -- they celebrated Assumption for us. From the 15th of August onwards, they sporadically shelled between 12 to 40 shells on the territory of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf. In January when a clash broke out between the ABiH and the HVO, the Serbs shelled the area more frequently, and sometime at the very beginning of the conflict some of their shells completely destroyed the main stations for supplying Gornji Vakuf with electricity. About the 20th of January, 1993, from that date onwards we didn't have electricity anymore in the entire area of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Batinic. You said that in the conflict in January, as far as you can remember, the HVO on the 22nd of January took control of the elevations that had previously been taken by the ABiH. You said that there were no more attacks on the town. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm now about to conclude. Let's go back to July 1993. Is it correct to say that in the second half of July 1993, from the 15th onwards, the ABiH attacked the HVO in Bugojno?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: As far as you know, how many civilians from Bugojno and how many HVO soldiers passed through Uskoplje in the direction of Rama around the 23rd, 4th, 5th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several thousand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Tell me, sir, on that occasion did the ABiH continue to advance in the direction of Uskoplje?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: And then on to Pavic Polje. Naturally, they wanted to reach Makljen and go further. According to the information you have, was there fierce fighting in that area at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the -- well, with regard to the HVO, Bugojno lost about the 20th of July, 1993, lost a lot, and from that day onwards the ABiH forces tried to take territory or areas in Gornji Vakuf where Croats lived.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Please, we have a problem when we say the 20th of 6th. It's --

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of July, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you. Now let's go back to the 31st and the 1st and so on. According to your information, was there complete breakdown of all the defence lines of the HVO in the town of Vakuf, in Uskoplje and around?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 80 per cent of the defence lines of the HVO on the evening between the 31st of July and the 1st of August were broken. These lines were lost, in fact.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is it true to say that the people and the soldiers started withdrawing in the direction of Rama on a massive scale?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, that's true.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that a number of people burnt their own houses? Croats did that. They killed their livestock, et cetera, when leaving that area?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Do you know that at the time I was in the area?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw each other, Mr. General, on the 1st of August in town.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that on the 1st of August we managed to retake all the lines?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Because I was a little boastful, is it true to say that I took the remainder of the troops back on a tank?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Pidris, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: What is not yet clear is what Croats, and religious Croats in particular, mean when they say "Assumption." What is this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Croatian Catholics in Bosnia and Herzegovina and throughout the world have a number of religious festivals which they celebrate, Christmas, Easter, and Assumption before all.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: My last question. At the repeater, there were two things. It was possible to broadcast the signal of TV Sarajevo 1 and TV Sarajevo 2.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Did the HVO ask that the part of the repeater broadcasting TV Sarajevo 2, which wasn't being broadcast anymore, did they ask for that part of the repeater to be used so that the Croatian programme in Zagreb could be watched?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the conclusion adopted by the Executive Committee.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Batinic. I wish you a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Praljak. We will now have our 20-minute break. Mr. Scott, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I'll be very brief, and you should know for the record I'm not taking anyone's time in saying this. But I will make the Prosecution's periodic objection and observation that I await the day, I await the day when anyone will be able to explain to me that that was cross-examination. We continue to object to this procedure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have our 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a technical issue. I thought I would handle it right now before we lose track of time. Today, we submitted an amended IC list for the witness Zelenika, and we added one document IC 00863. So that's just to -- for technical purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have the same sort of thing to say. The Petkovic Defence also submitted an annex to the formal list of exhibits shown to the witness Mirko Zelenika. The extra document concerns a map, and IC number is 00862. Thank you very much. And if I could continue immediately, since it's my turn to cross-examine the witness. I would first of all like to greet the Chamber, everyone else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you, Mr. Batinic. My name is Vesna Alaburic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Concerning the initial list submitted by the Prlic Defence team, it shall be given Exhibit number IC 00879, and the supplementary list submitted by the Petkovic Defence team shall be given Exhibit number IC 00880. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, my name is Vesna Alaburic. I'm a lawyer from Zagreb, and I am defending General Milivoj Petkovic in this trial. Could you first inform the Chamber whether we know each other? Have we ever spoken to each other before today, participate in your proofing for this testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know you from before, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Batinic, could you clarify something for us, something that I thought was not sufficiently clear? When answering a question put to you by my colleague Karnavas about removing check-points in villages, the honourable Judge Trechsel then put a question to you and asked you why those check-points in the villages had been removed. You answered that the reason was to make it possible for people to move around freely in the area of Gornji Vakuf, but you said that three check-points were to remain at the entrance to Gornji Vakuf. Now, this was entered into the transcript on page 11. Do you remember that answer?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What is unclear to me in your answer is the following: If the check-points in villages were removed to make it possible for people to move around freely in the area of Gornji Vakuf, the question remains: What was the purpose of the three check-points at the entrance to Gornji Vakuf? Someone could draw the conclusion that those check-points remained there to prevent people from moving around freely, and perhaps one might think that the check-points were there for security reasons. So, Mr. Batinic, could you please clarify the matter for us?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very simple. Before there were any incidents in Gornji Vakuf municipality, the HVO and the TO - I'm talking about the armed forces - had joint check-points at entrances or access routes to the town and municipality of Gornji Vakuf. The check-point from the direction of Bugojno in Gornji Vakuf municipality area was in the Humac settlement, which is about ten kilometres from the actual town of Gornji Vakuf. The check-point from the direction of Novi Travnik towards the direction of -- the entrance to settlements in the area of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf was in the settlement of Bistrica -- or, rather, it controlled the entrance from the canyon of the Bistrik River, from the entrance to Gornji Vakuf; and the check-point from Prozor at the entrance to Gornji Vakuf at the very entrance of Gornji Vakuf was also a joint check-point. Our order had to do with removing check-points inside settlements in the very municipality of Gornji Vakuf, which is where you had a settlement where the majority were Muslims, and then you had one settlement where the Croats were in the majority, and that's how it went on, in an alternate manner. These check-points had to be removed, but the three main check-points, well, they were used to control entrance and exit of any individuals to and from the area of our municipality. And also, it was to prevent conscripts from leaving the municipality if they didn't have certificates from the TO, the HVO, and the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, at these three main check-points, were soldiers from the HVO and the ABiH, did they act in the same way towards Muslims and Croats, or was there discrimination on a national basis?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't behave in a different manner. They treated them in an identical manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You mentioned military conscripts, and we have seen a document that concerns military conscripts. I'll have a question about this for you. Perhaps you know the answer, perhaps not. In Gornji Vakuf, was there a record of military conscripts which included young men regardless of their ethnic origin, or were various kinds of records kept for military conscripts? Tell me if you know.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war in Gornji Vakuf, we just had one single record of military conscripts. The secretary for national defence kept these records. At the beginning of the very war, the list of military conscripts recognised by the operational headquarters of the Croatian people, which was founded by decision of the Crisis Staff of the HDZ for the municipality of Gornji Vakuf, well, had its own list of Croatian military conscripts, and the SDA had a list of its own conscripts -- or, rather, the Patriotic League also had such a list.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back for a moment to this road. Was Gornji Vakuf an important communication place, or was Gornji Vakuf insignificant in terms of communications?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depending on the viewpoint. For us, it was an important transport location in view of the fact that from Gornji Vakuf you could go to Central Bosnia and towards the south to Herzegovina. So the Bugojno-Gornji Vakuf-Prozor road going on to Jablanica and Mostar, and on the other hand, Gornji Vakuf-Bugojno-Travnik, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I would now like to show you a part of the statement of a witness who was a British soldier in the UNPROFOR unit deployed in Gornji Vakuf. The page is 8468 of the transcript, and he said: "Who controls Gornji Vakuf also controls the entire approach to that part of Bosnia." Would you agree with this statement of his?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But viewed from the south towards Bosnia, from Herzegovina towards Bosnia, this area of Gornji Vakuf viewed geographically is in Bosnia, and the neighbouring municipality of Rama is already in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, from Mostar towards Bugojno, could there any other -- was there any other way to reach it except via Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, via Kupres, but at that time Kupres was occupied.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the possibilities at that time. After the occupation of Kupres, could one reach Bugojno in any other way except via Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, could you reach Novi Travnik and Travnik from Mostar without passing through Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you now as a man who is local to Gornji Vakuf. This same British soldier, in answer to a question from Judge Antonetti about the possibility of having control over particular areas, said that even if the HVO would have the control of the road from Gornji Vakuf towards Bugojno or Prozor, it would not be sufficiently important unless he had control of the localities close to the road, and he mentioned the names Uzricje, Hrasnica, Zdrimci, because the army that was in those villages and has visual communication with these roads could hinder movement along that road. Let me repeat the names of the villages which are mentioned in the transcript. Uzricje, the villages of Uzricje, Hrasnica - Hrasnica - and Zdrimci, on page 8474 of the transcript. Tell me, Mr. Batinic, according to your knowledge of the area, is this statement true or not?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is partly true.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, which part of it is true and which is not?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uzricje is at least a kilometre away from the road Gornji Vakuf-Bugojno or Gornji Vakuf-Prozor. Hrasnica leans on the Gornji Vakuf-Bugojno road, and Zdrimci is at least 500 metres away from the road, from the Gornji Vakuf-Prozor road. And I must note that from Zdrimci, the road could be controlled from the elevation point Babe [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: There's no dispute those villages are not on the road. They are removed from the road.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This road could not be controlled from Uzricje in any possible way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could another important road be controlled from Uzricje?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the Croatian part of Gornji Vakuf, there is a forest road which passes through Uzricje going to Mackovac or Pidris.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this side road, was it very important for Prozor-Gornji Vakuf communication in the event that the ABiH could prevent communication from Mackovac towards Gornji Vakuf and Bugojno? In other words, could this side-road be used to reach Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Prozor-Vakuf road is blocked, then the only way to reach Mackovac and Pidris from Gornji Vakuf would be the road going through Uzricje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. That was what I expected you to tell us. Could we now have a look at the first conflict, which happened on the 20th of June, 1992. You spoke at length about this conflict. It is the conflict in June. We've also seen a number of documents from that period when the Presidency of Gornji Vakuf issued orders to both the HVO and the TO. Do you remember those documents and the discussions about this?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it right to believe that those documents show that in those days in 1992 the HVO fully cooperated with the ABiH and that they functioned as the joint armed force of Bosnia-Herzegovina, if I can put it that way, or could those documents be given some other meaning?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no other meaning. The HVO and the Territorial Defence -- or, rather, the armed forces of these two components acted in a coordinated fashion along the defence lines against the Serb aggressor, and they cooperated well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us now see whether this situation was of a purely local nature, or was it of any broader significance for this part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So please look at my set of documents, document 4D 397. It is a document which is already an exhibit. It is a letter by Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic addressed on the 20th of June, 1991, to the Municipal Staff of the HVO in Gornji Vakuf. Have you found that document?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's a brief document. In the fourth line, Brigadier Petkovic says that the TO and the HVO are component parts of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Mr. Batinic, could you please comment on this? Does this statement correspond to what we saw in the documents of the Presidency of Gornji Vakuf, which apply simultaneously to the Territorial Defence and the HVO?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff of Gornji Vakuf and the Presidency of Gornji Vakuf municipality considered as legitimate defence forces both the HVO and the TO as equally and on an equal footing. And let me add that as the Presidency of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf, by our decision we appointed to the Presidency the commander of the armed forces of the HVO and the commander of the armed forces of the TO who, let me add in passing, regularly attended our meetings. Sometimes one of their deputies would attend, and they would regularly report the same body about the situation on the ground, the behaviour of the aggressor, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: On the basis of those documents and your statement, one could get the impression that in Gornji Vakuf you managed to establish something like a Joint Command. Would such a conclusion be correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could not say that there was a Joint Command, but what one can say is that they coordinated their activities, that is, the command of the HVO and the TO command. So their coordination was excellent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we look at the last sentence in this document of Brigadier Petkovic at the time, which ends with the call to go jointly to the line of defence against the common enemy, that is, the Bosnian Serbs, would this call be in accordance with what was happening in the area of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in view of the fact that the armed forces of the TO had abandoned the defence line facing the Serbs on Radusa mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of questions regarding the conflict in October 1992. This is the second conflict that you mentioned. Please look at two documents. The first is P 633. It is also a letter by Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, who now has the position of chief of the HVO Main Staff, and it is addressed, among others, to Gornji Vakuf urging the commanders to try and calm the situation. And the next document, P 644, dated the 24th of October, with roughly the same contents, and it is an order to establish contact with the party in conflict and a cessation of hostilities. Tell me, Mr. Batinic, you didn't see these orders before?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic was?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my memory serves me well, he was the commander of the HVO in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you know about him at the time, that is in June and October 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard of General Petkovic, but I didn't have occasion to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: These orders to calm the situation and to cease hostilities, do they correspond to what was going on in the area of Gornji Vakuf at the time, that is, that the local commanders were endeavouring to calm the situation and ease tensions?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely so, the more so as we in Gornji Vakuf made a maximum of effort to avoid that conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did the commanders of the TO and the HVO occasionally walk through town together so as to let the people know that they were together, that they were endeavouring to control the situation and in that sense to set the population at ease regarding the situation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the two commanders of the armed forces but a group of maybe up to 50 men in which there were equal numbers of Croats and Muslims, the most influential people of Gornji Vakuf, which included the commanders of the armed forces of the HVO and the TO. And we had the so-called March of Peace throughout the town of Gornji Vakuf, and by this peace march we wanted to bring peace to the population of Gornji Vakuf to see that we were together, that nothing strange would happen or should happen, especially not a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us precisely when this peace march took place?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this peace march took place in the evening of the 24th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, let me ask you a few brief questions about flags. You spoke about this at length. If my understanding was correct, it was customary for the Croats to hoist their Croatian flags [as interpreted] during the holidays. Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did this custom exist prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the first multi-party elections, this could be done freely for our holidays that I mentioned, that is Christmas, New Year, and the Holy Three Kings. Unfortunately, prior to the multi-party elections, this was not allowed in Socialist Yugoslavia and in Gornji Vakuf at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The elections were at the end of 1990, so from the end of 1990 onwards the Croats of Bosnia-Herzegovina could freely hang up their flags; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the appropriate holidays.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In 1991 when the flag of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina was hoisted, would any Muslim inhabitants consider this flag to be a provocation?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the Holy Three Kings frequently. Maybe this is common knowledge, but nevertheless, let us say when this holiday occurs. It is on the 6th of January. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And finally, let me just ask you something in connection with a few documents of the BH army and some other Muslim documents, so please look at document 3D 511. These are conclusions from a meeting of representatives of the Muslims held on the 11th of July, 1992, in Gornji Vakuf. I'm interested in paragraph 4. Please tell us first whether you were aware that a meeting of the representatives of Muslims was being held on at that date in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could there be a pause, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at paragraph 4. "The representatives of Muslims of Central Bosnia and Herzegovina approve and support the fight of the HVO as a component part --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You're going too fast, much too fast. It's often happens when one reads a document. The interpreters have difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I thought I was slow enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So paragraph 4, the first sentence: "The representatives of the Muslims of Central Bosnia and Herzegovina approve and support the fight of the HVO as a component part of the entire liberating army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in all military issues." Mr. Batinic, could you please comment on this? According to your knowledge and the positions of your co-inhabitants of Muslim ethnicity, did they support the efforts of the HVO, and was it challenged at all that the HVO was defending Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Muslims in Gornji Vakuf perceived the armed forces of the HVO and the armed forces of the TO in the same way. Their duty was to defend the Gornji Vakuf municipality. The most responsible representatives of the Muslim people who were in the Crisis Staff and in the Presidency of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf showed this in their opinions, in their decisions, in their conclusions on a daily basis. This was confirmed on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Batinic, I'll now show you a document, P 1226. It's already been admitted into evidence, so if you could just comment on part of it, please. In this trial, it's very important for us to know whether the Muslim population of certain villages in Gornji Vakuf moved out of their villages, and if they did so, how. So please comment on the penultimate paragraph in this report from Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. I'll read out the sentence that I'm interested in: "The upper part of town and all the villages inhabited by Muslims are under the control of the Armija, of the army, with the exception of the village of Uzricje, Uzricje, part of whose residents evacuated or moved out voluntarily and moved to Gornji Vakuf, as well as the village of Hrasnica whose residents evacuated to Grnica." Mr. Batinic, do you know who Enver Hadzihasanovic was?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the time, I did not know who Mr. -- I don't even know what his surname is. Hadzihasanovic. I later heard about him from commanders of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was Gornji Vakuf in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I had, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time - and this includes the post-war period - hear that Muslims evacuated from these individual villages around Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what happened exactly on the 19th of January, 1993, in these inhabited places. I have already said, I said so yesterday and I have said so today, that during that period of time I was located or deployed in the settlement Gornji Vakuf below the elevations, the repeater, and the purpose I had was to protect myself and my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. I thought that perhaps you had heard something about the post-war periods and events. Can you just comment on 4D 1235 now, please. It's a brief document, a short document. It's a report from Commander Hadzihasanovic dated the 10th of January, 1993, so a period prior to the beginning of the conflict. It says and I quote: "Given the continuation of the Geneva political negotiations -- on the occasion of political negotiations in Geneva and at the request of a huge number of units and fighters of the 3rd Corps of the ABiH, we hereby offer you our unconditional support in your efforts to prevent the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina on ethnic or any other principles. "Do not allow --" I haven't finish the quote. I'm continuing. "Do not allow the following, and neither shall we, do not allow that the blood spilled so far and the sacrifice of our fighters, children, women, fathers and mothers be in vain." Mr. Batinic, tell us, have you ever heard of any period of time -- at the time and later that members of the ABiH were against organising Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the Vance-Owen Plan that had been put forward in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to the period that this document refers to, the 10th of January, 1993, well, I had no such information.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And later on, did you obtain any such information?

utterances.speaker: ZDRAVKO BATINIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, when you're a participant in armed combat and when your life is at threat on a daily basis, your main task is to remain alive and then to protect those who are with you, and you are least concerned with such matters as these before us. So I can't say anything in answer to your question. If they had accepted one of the solutions, the war between the ABiH and the HVO wouldn't have been so fierce.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Batinic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have now completed my cross-examination. There is just one correction I would like to make, and I thank Ms. Pinter for telling me about this. On page 86, line 11 and 12, my question on the flag of the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina was wrongly translated as a question about the Croatian flag. So please bear in mind that I always asked questions about the Croatian flag of the Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have a few minutes before we adjourn; and therefore, it's perhaps not necessary for the Prosecution to commence with their re-examination unless they so desire. If not, we can start with cross-examination tomorrow at 9.00. The Prosecution will have four hours. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. No, we agree with you, Your Honour. We would appreciate that -- since we only have about ten minutes, we'll appreciate if we could just make a clean start tomorrow. I will use one moment of the time, if I may, please, to ask for a -- the Court's permission to file a longer response to the applications for provisional release. Just as a brief recap, Your Honours, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I won't mention any names, but I understand. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
